chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding the sacrificial animal (udhiyah) whose horn is broken, he (peace be upon him) said: 'When the interior horn is sound, it suffices.'

key_terms.الْأُضْحِيَّةُ: Sacrificial animal offered during Eid al-Adha

ai.seo_question: Is a sacrificial animal valid if its horn is broken?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the specific criteria for defects in sacrificial animals, emphasizing that the integrity of the horn's root determines validity rather than the tip. In Shia fiqh, this ruling underscores the principle that minor imperfections do not invalidate the ritual unless they significantly impair the animal's utility or appearance, reflecting the juristic focus on ease and practicality in worship. It serves as a foundational text for distinguishing between permissible minor flaws and those that render the udhiyah unacceptable.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Jameel,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> regarding the sacrificial animal whose horn is broken. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘When it was such that its interior horn was correct, so it would suffice’.
en.sarwar: 13. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Jamil who has said the following: “I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the animal for offering which has a broken horn.
He (the Imam) said, ‘If the horn inside is well, then it is sufficient.’”
